design.quote: Ketamine, an anesthetic available since 1970, and esketamine, its newer S‐enantiomer, provide a novel approach for the treatment of depression and other psychiatric disorders. At subanesthetic doses, the two drugs, along with their older congener, phencyclidine (PCP), induce a transient, altered mental state by blocking the N‐methyl‐D‐aspartate (NMDA) receptor for glutamate, the primary excitatory neurotransmitter in the mammalian central nervous system.

findings.quote: Direct effects of PCP, an even more potent NMDA antagonist than ketamine, were less systematically measured since it was primarily an illicit street drug in the late 1960s and 1970s.
